text:
The response provides accurate, practical, and well-organized guidance covering the essential pillars of Japanese business etiquette—greetings, business card exchange, punctuality, dress code, gift-giving, and dining. The advice is actionable and culturally appropriate for a general overview. However, it lacks deeper nuance regarding hierarchical dynamics (e.g., who bows first, seating arrangements), the importance of indirect communication and consensus-building (*nemawashi*), the role of after-work socializing (*nomikai*), and specific protocols like keeping business cards on the table during meetings rather than immediately pocketing them. While suitable as an introductory guide, it could be more comprehensive regarding the subtle power structures and group-oriented mindset central to Japanese business culture.

Rating: [[8]]
